rag_hits.title: Flood Resilience at NYCHA — Lessons Learned
rag_hits.text: Letter from the Vice President for Recovery & Resilience Dear New Yorkers, Hurricane Sandy devasted New York City in October 2012. Despite living in a city with 520 miles of coastline, residents had never grappled with storm surge at this scale. Salt water and debris covered huge swaths of the five boroughs, including many NYCHA campuses. Unlike prior major storms, the impacts didn’t dissipate when the weather improved. Salt water corroded critical infrastructure that was stored below grade. The homes of tens of thousands of public housing residents—most of whom couldn’t evacuate before the storm—were without water, power, heat, hot water, or elevator service for weeks.

rag_hits.title: MTA Climate Resilience Roadmap (October 2025 update)
rag_hits.citation: MTA Climate Resilience Roadmap, October 2025 update
rag_hits.text: II. Adapting to Extreme Weather Threats 17 Climate Resilience Roadmap - 2025 Update16 4 Ave between Union St and 36 St, Brooklyn – This stretch of 4 Avenue Brooklyn is served by five stations that have been impacted by heavy rainfall: Union St r , 4 Av-9 St r , Prospect Av r , 25 St r , and 36 St d nr . Why City action is needed: This area of the Gowanus neighborhood is prone to chronic flooding and is also under-sewered. NYCDEP has made investments in the Gowanus neighborhood and we urge additional investment to further alleviate flooding. What the MTA is doing: We have installed elevated steps at entrances to help mitigate flooding impacts from street and sidewalk stormwater runoff.

This is an automated hazard-exposure briefing produced by Riprap from live and baked data sources. It is informational only and not a substitute for a professional risk assessment.

**In brief.**
This address is outside the 2012 Sandy inundation footprint [sandy_inundation], in FEMA flood zone X [fema_nfhl], and outside the modeled flooding in the DEP stormwater scenarios for current, 2050 and 2080 sea-level rise [dep_moderate_current][dep_moderate_2050][dep_extreme_2080]. 34 flood-related 311 complaints were filed within 200 m in the last 5 years [nyc311].

**Hazard Reader.**
This address sits outside the empirical 2012 Hurricane Sandy inundation footprint (NYC OEM) [sandy_inundation]. This address sits in FEMA flood zone X, per NFHL FIRM panel 3604970352F, effective 2007 [fema_nfhl]. NYC DEP stormwater scenarios at this address: current sea level with 2.13 in/hr of rain, outside the modeled flooding [dep_moderate_current]; 2050 sea-level rise with 2.13 in/hr, outside the modeled flooding [dep_moderate_2050]; 2080 sea-level rise with 3.66 in/hr, outside the modeled flooding [dep_extreme_2080]. No Hurricane Ida (Sept 2021) high-water marks were surveyed within 800 m of this address [ida_hwm]. Nearest USGS-surveyed mark: Coney Island Ave., between Ave. P and Ave. O, Midwood, Brooklyn (1351 m away) [ida_hwm]. Experimental: msradam/Prithvi-EO-2.0-NYC-Pluvial on Sentinel-2 scenes from 2021-09-02, compared with 2021-08-13: 0 m² of new surface water within 500 m of this address (100% of that circle observed); 0.00% of Madison showed new water (100% of it observed) [prithvi_water]. Street and basement flooding drains within hours and is not visible at 10 to 20 m, so no water here is not evidence of no flooding [prithvi_water]. Elevation 6.56 m; this point is higher than 49% of the ground within 200 m (the 49th percentile; a low percentile means a local low spot where water collects); HAND (height above the nearest drainage channel) 3.52 m; TWI (topographic wetness index; higher means water tends to collect) 10.28 [microtopo]. Local basin relief (the rise from this point to the highest ground within 750 m): 1.48 m [microtopo]. Experimental: Policy passages retrieved from the NYC flood-policy corpus for this place: 3 (embedding retrieval; entity tags are experimental) [policy_corpus].

**Live Observer.**
No FloodNet sensors deployed within 600 m of this address [floodnet]. 34 NYC 311 flood-related complaints filed within 200 m of this location in the last 5 years: 16 catch basin, 12 sewer backup, 6 street flooding [nyc311]. Latest METAR at JFK Airport, NY (15.6 km away): 16.0°C (obs 2026-09-29T01:25) [nws_obs]. Latest reading at The Battery, NY: 5.92 ft above MLLW (+1.04 ft vs predicted tide), observed 2026-09-28 21:30 [noaa_tides]. No active USGS stream gauge reported a stage reading in the last 2 days within about 10 to 14 km of this address [usgs_gauges].

**Asset Register.**
5 MTA subway entrances within 800 m of this address: 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 3 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [mta_entrance_exposure]. 0 NYCHA developments within 2000 m of this address: 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 0 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [nycha_development_exposure]. 1 NYC DOE schools within 1500 m of this address: 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 1 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [doe_school_exposure]. 3 hospitals within 3000 m of this address: 1 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 2 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [doh_hospital_exposure].

**Projector.**
No active NWS flood / coastal / wind alerts at this point [nws_alerts]. Experimental: a TTM model fine-tuned on Battery gauge history, with no wind or pressure input, forecasts a peak surge residual of 0.37 m at The Battery about 5 h ahead [ttm_battery_surge]. Use NOAA ETSS or the Stevens Flood Advisory System for storm decisions. Experimental: 9 flood-related 311 complaints within 200 m over the last 512 days; a zero-shot TTM forecast with no rainfall input and no backtest projects about 0.1 per week for the next 96 days [ttm_311_forecast]. NPCC4 (2024) projects sea-level rise at the Battery of 0.38 m (15 in) by the 2050s and 0.79 m (31 in) by 2100 at the median, relative to 2000-2004; 90th percentile 0.74 m and 1.65 m [npcc4_slr].
